title: World-Class Long-Distance Running Performances Are Best Predicted by Volume of Easy Runs and Deliberate Practice of Short-Interval and Tempo Runs
authors: Casado A, Hanley B, Santos-Concejero J, Ruiz-Perez LM
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: 85 elite-standard and world-class male long-distance runners, training reported after 3, 5 and 7 years
findings: Total distance correlated strongly with performance (r >= 0.75, p<0.001) and explained significant variance (R2 >= 0.57).
Easy runs (r >= 0.68), tempo runs (r >= 0.50) and short intervals (r >= 0.53) correlated with performance; long intervals did not (r >= 0.22).
Hierarchical regression: easy runs and tempo runs accounted for significant variance (p<0.01).
Authors note easy running was crucial partly because of its contribution to total distance.
limitations: Elite and world-class men only, retrospective self-reported bests, correlational, track-event scoring; weak generalisation to recreational and ultra runners.
implications: Fill added volume with easy continuous running; keep tempo and short intervals as a modest fixed share.
Do not prioritise long intervals for volume-limited athletes.
